definitions.explanation: Small sardines or anchovies that have been boiled and dried, used primarily to make dashi (soup stock). A fundamental ingredient in Japanese home cooking.

examples.japanese: {煮干|にぼ}しでだし⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧。
⟦{味噌汁|みそしる}→味噌汁：04954_misoshiru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧だし⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{煮干|にぼ}し⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Dried sardines are often used for miso soup broth.

examples.japanese: {煮干|にぼ}し⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{内臓|ないぞう}→内臓：05028_naizou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}って→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{浸|つ}けておく⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{雑味|ざつみ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧だし⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{取|と}れる→取れる：02376_toreru⟧。
examples.english: If you remove the heads and innards of the dried sardines and soak them in water beforehand, you can make a clean-tasting broth.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Literally "⟦{煮|に}る→煮る：01971_niru⟧ (to boil) + ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧ (to dry)" — describing the production process of boiling small fish and then drying them.

USAGE:
{煮干|にぼ}しだし is one of the main types of Japanese soup stock, alongside ⟦{鰹節|かつおぶし}→鰹節：04935_katsuobushi⟧ (bonito flake) dashi and ⟦{昆布|こんぶ}→昆布：04934_konbu⟧ (kelp) dashi. It produces a more robust, fishy flavor and is particularly common in ⟦{味噌汁|みそしる}→味噌汁：04954_misoshiru⟧.

Also called いりこ in western Japan, especially in the Kansai and Shikoku regions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {煮干|にぼ}しだし: sardine broth
- {煮干|にぼ}しでだし⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to make broth from dried sardines
- {煮干|にぼ}し⟦ラーメン→ラーメン：05181_raamen⟧: sardine-broth ramen
